articles.title: Lotofácil da Independência: confira os números sorteados | G1
articles.standfirst: Concurso 3780 foi realizado nesta terça-feira (15), às 21h e não acumula. Prêmio é estimado em R$ 300 milhões.
articles.summary: Concurso especial foi realizado nesta terça-feira (15), às 21h e não acumula. Prêmio estimado em R$ 300 milhões.
articles.body:
Volante da Lotofácil da Independência. — Foto: Reprodução/Caixa

O sorteio da Lotofácil da Independência 2026 , do concurso 3780, foi realizado nesta terça-feira (15), em São Paulo. O prêmio para as apostas que acertarem as quinze dezenas é estimado em R$ 300 milhões. Setenta e duas apostas acertaram os 15 números e vão levar R$ 4.488.579 cada.

Veja os números sorteados: 01 - 02 - 03 - 04 - 05 - 06 - 07 - 12 - 15 - 16 - 17 - 19 - 21 - 22 - 23

15 acertos: 72 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 4.488.579,00

14 acertos : 8978 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 2.762,74

13 acertos : 290866 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 17,50

12 acertos : 3465636 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 7,00

11 acertos: 19323208 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 3,50

A Lotofácil da Independência é realizada anualmente em setembro e chega, em 2026, à sua 15ª edição.

Resultado da Lotofácil da Independência. — Foto: Reprodução/Caixa

Na Lotofácil , o apostador escolhe entre 15 e 20 números, de 1 a 25. No sorteio, são retirados 15 números, sem repetição. Ganha o prêmio principal quem acertar os 15 números sorteados, mas também há premiação para apostas com 11, 12, 13 ou 14 acertos. Quando há mais de um ganhador em uma faixa, o valor do prêmio é dividido entre os vencedores.

A aposta simples, com 15 dezenas, custa R$ 3,50.

articles.title: Nagpur horror: Woman’s car crashes into pavement, 5 injured; locals demand arrest
articles.summary: Nagpur: Woman allegedly drunk drives into pavement in Gittikhadan, injuring 4 children; 2-year-old critical. Protests erupt, police begin FIR process.
articles.body: NAGPUR: A car rashly driven by a woman ploughed into the pavement, where children were playing near Gond Mohalla between Gittikhadan Chowk and Dinshaw factory late Tuesday night.Of the five critically injured, one is a two-year-old kid, Vanshika Kulmethe, and her uncle. Eyewitnesses said, the woman was driving under the influence of liquor. The accident triggered massive public outrage even as the injured battled for life at hospital.By midnight, over 500 residents of Gond Mohalla and adjoining areas laid siege to the Gittikhadan police station, demanding immediate arrest of the woman driver.The mob wrecked the woman’s car even as cops kept the woman driver hidden in the police station to shield her from public wrath. Senior officers rushed to the spot and heavy bandobast was deployed.The woman, reportedly from an affluent family, has been rounded up, though she is yet to be named accused, till reports last came in. The process of registering the offence is underway. Locals insisted she must be named in an FIR for rash driving and endangering lives. Police are investigating the case and assured strict action. articles.title: Bem-Estar #368 - Como evitar o mofo dentro de casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Umidade chega a 100% em dias de chuva e, com pouco sol, favorece fungos que podem causar danos materiais e trazer consequências para a saúde.
articles.summary: Umidade chega a 100% em dias de chuva e, com pouco sol, favorece fungos que podem causar danos materiais e trazer consequências para a saúde.
articles.body:
Este mês de setembro já é o mais chuvoso da cidade de São Paulo desde 1943, segundo dados do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia. A sequência de dias chuvosos aumenta também a umidade do ar que fica em torno de 80 a 90% e pode chegar a 100 quando está chovendo. Com pouco sol, a água não evapora direito e as casas ficam úmidas, com paredes molhadas, espelhos e janelas embaçados, roupas que não secam... todas as condições que contribuem para o aparecimento de mofo.

Além dos danos materiais, o mofo traz consequências para a saúde. Como prevenir e acabar com o mofo dentro de casa? Este é o tema do videocast do Bem-Estar desta quarta-feira (16) e a nossa convidada é a bióloga Karen Signori.

articles.title: UNIFAE conquista recurso do MEC para fortalecer Cursinho Popular | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto integra a Rede Nacional de Cursinhos Populares e oferece aos estudantes preparação gratuita para o ENEM e vestibulares.
articles.summary: Projeto integra a Rede Nacional de Cursinhos Populares e oferece aos estudantes preparação gratuita para o ENEM e vestibulares.
articles.body:
Projeto integra a Rede Nacional de Cursinhos Populares e oferece aos estudantes preparação gratuita para o ENEM e vestibulares — Foto: Crédito: Arquivo pessoal.

A busca por mais oportunidades de acesso ao ensino superior ganhou um importante reforço em São João da Boa Vista neste ano. Por meio de uma proposta elaborada e submetida pela Pró-Reitoria de Extensão (PROEX), a UNIFAE conquistou a aprovação do Cursinho Popular Sanjoanense no Edital CPOP nº 01/2026, do Ministério da Educação (MEC).

Com a aprovação, o projeto passou a integrar a Rede Nacional de Cursinhos Populares e recebeu um investimento de R$ 132.390,00, recurso que permite ampliar e qualificar as atividades oferecidas aos estudantes que se preparam gratuitamente para o ENEM e os principais vestibulares.

Mais do que um reconhecimento institucional, a conquista representa um investimento direto na trajetória dos jovens que participam do Cursinho. Os recursos possibilitam fortalecer a estrutura do projeto e criar condições para que os estudantes tenham maior suporte durante sua preparação para o ingresso no ensino superior.

Uma das iniciativas viabilizadas pelo edital é o Auxílio Permanência, destinado aos estudantes regularmente matriculados no Cursinho Popular Sanjoanense. A medida contribui para que os alunos possam permanecer no projeto durante o ano e seguir sua preparação com melhores condições.

Uma conquista construída pela UNIFAE e seus parceiros

A iniciativa é fruto de uma construção coletiva entre as instituições parceiras do Cursinho Popular Sanjoanense: Câmara Municipal, por meio do vereador Leandro Thomazine, Prefeitura de São João da Boa Vista, Departamento de Educação, UNIFAE, UNESP, Instituto Federal e Academia de Letras.

Para a Pró-Reitora de Extensão da UNIFAE, Profa. Dra. Anita Bellotto Leme Nagib, a aprovação demonstra a importância de aproximar a Universidade das necessidades da comunidade.

“A aprovação nesse edital reafirma o papel estratégico da extensão universitária como ferramenta de transformação social, contribuindo diretamente para o desenvolvimento educacional e para a construção de um futuro com mais equidade de oportunidades”, afirmou.

O Reitor da UNIFAE, Prof. Dr. Marco Aurélio Ferreira, também destaca que a conquista é resultado da união entre diferentes instituições em torno de um objetivo comum.

“Esse reconhecimento demonstra a força da união entre as entidades comprometidas com a educação pública de qualidade. Agradecemos a todos os parceiros que acreditaram e contribuíram com essa construção coletiva, que certamente terá impacto significativo na vida de muitos estudantes e no desenvolvimento da nossa comunidade”, destacou.

As aulas do Cursinho Popular Sanjoanense ocorrem no Campus principal da UNIFAE, de segunda a sexta-feira, das 18h45 às 22h45 — Foto: Crédito: ASCOM / UNIFAE.

Atualmente, o Cursinho Popular Sanjoanense atende dezenas de estudantes, oferecendo aulas gratuitas de segunda a sexta-feira, das 18h45 às 22h45, na UNIFAE.

A proposta é voltada a jovens e adultos oriundos da escola pública, estudantes bolsistas integrais da rede privada e pessoas de baixa renda familiar. A preparação contempla as quatro áreas do conhecimento avaliadas pelo ENEM: Linguagens, Ciências Humanas, Ciências da Natureza e Matemática.

Mas a formação vai além da preparação para uma prova. O Cursinho também busca ampliar o repertório cultural e cidadão dos estudantes, apresentar diferentes possibilidades de carreira e aproximá-los do universo acadêmico.

Ao longo do ano, os alunos também participam de atividades que proporcionam contato com a estrutura universitária e diferentes áreas profissionais. Na UNIFAE, por exemplo, já tiveram a oportunidade de conhecer laboratórios, espaços acadêmicos e possibilidades de formação profissional.

Para muitos desses estudantes, o Cursinho representa a oportunidade de ter acesso a uma preparação que, de outra forma, poderia estar fora de suas possibilidades financeiras.

É justamente nesse ponto que o investimento conquistado pela UNIFAE junto ao MEC ganha significado: transformar uma iniciativa local em uma política de ampliação de oportunidades, oferecendo mais condições para que estudantes possam sonhar com a universidade — e, principalmente, se preparar para chegar até ela.

O Centro Universitário UNIFAE de São João da Boa Vista, localizado a 245 km de São Paulo, chega aos 65 anos num momento histórico de transformação: inovação nas propostas pedagógicas, mais laboratórios, investimentos em infraestrutura, modernização de equipamentos e, principalmente, uma nova mentalidade com ênfase na participação como processo de construção coletiva, sempre reafirmando seu compromisso de ser uma referência regional na Educação.

O Vestibular 2027 da UNIFAE está com inscrições abertas até 13 de outubro, com bolsas de estudo de até 100% em 17 cursos nas áreas de Exatas, Humanas e Saúde. A prova presencial será em 18 de outubro, às 9h da manhã, no Campus Principal – Largo Engenheiro Paulo de Almeida Sandeville, n° 15, Jd. Santo André – São João da Boa Vista-SP.

Mais informações o site: vestibular.fae.br

articles.title: Ataque de drone russo mata 5 em ônibus de passageiros na Ucrânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente Volodymyr Zelensky chamou o ataque de 'atrocidade'; trem com cerca de 170 passageiros também foi atingido.
articles.summary: Presidente Volodymyr Zelenskyy chamou o ataque de “atrocidade”; trem com cerca de 170 passageiros também foi atingido nesta quarta-feira
articles.body:
Nesta foto, fornecida pelo Serviço de Emergência da Ucrânia, bombeiros combatem um incêndio em casas particulares após um ataque aéreo russo em Sumy, na Ucrânia. — Foto: Serviço de Emergênia da Ucrânia via AP

Um ataque de drone russo atingiu um ônibus de passageiros no sul da Ucrânia nesta quarta-feira (16). Cinco pessoas morreram e ao menos sete ficaram feridas , segundo autoridades ucranianas.

O ataque ocorreu no distrito de Nikopol, na região de Dnipropetrovsk, próximo à linha de frente no sul do país. Segundo Oleksandr Hanzha, chefe da administração militar regional, os cinco mortos estavam no local quando as equipes de emergência chegaram. Os feridos foram levados para atendimento médico.

O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky , chamou o ataque de “atrocidade”. Em uma publicação na rede social X, ele afirmou que o veículo era um micro-ônibus e que o ataque “não tinha justificativa militar”.

Segundo Zelenskyy, a ação faz parte de uma série de ataques russos contra meios de transporte e infraestrutura logística e crítica da Ucrânia. Ele afirmou que esses ataques continuam de forma ininterrupta.

Na região de Mykolaiv, um trem de passageiros também foi atingido nesta quarta. Uma estação ferroviária e uma locomotiva a diesel foram danificadas. Cerca de 170 passageiros que estavam no trem foram retirados antes do ataque, segundo Zelenskyy.

Uma locomotiva elétrica também foi atingida na cidade de Kovel, no noroeste da Ucrânia.

Ucrânia pede locomotivas a países aliados

Os ataques russos danificaram ou destruíram mais de 500 locomotivas ucranianas desde o início da guerra, em fevereiro de 2022, segundo o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha. Mais da metade desses ataques teria ocorrido neste ano.

Sybiha afirmou que os ataques à rede ferroviária são sistemáticos e têm como objetivo prejudicar a logística do país. Ele pediu que países aliados ajudem a Ucrânia a obter locomotivas compatíveis com sua malha ferroviária e a financiar a reposição dos equipamentos destruídos.

Em outra publicação, o ministro afirmou que as forças russas atingem trens de passageiros , locomotivas, estações e linhas ferroviárias “sabendo exatamente” da importância dessas estruturas para civis, evacuações e para a economia ucraniana.

articles.title: Coreia do Norte condena acordo de defesa entre EUA e Coreia do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Pyongyang afirmou que pacto para ampliar cooperação contra armas de destruição em massa aumenta o risco de uso desses armamentos na região
articles.summary: Pyongyang afirmou que pacto para ampliar cooperação contra armas de destruição em massa aumenta o risco de uso desses armamentos na região.
articles.body:
Da esquerda para a direita: presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, presidente da Coreia do Sul, Lee Jae-myung, e presidente da Coreia do Norte, Kim Jong-un. — Foto: Mark Schiefelbein/AP/Annabelle Gordon/REUTERS/KCNA

O Ministério da Defesa da Coreia do Norte condenou nesta quarta-feira (16) um acordo entre Estados Unidos e Coreia do Sul para ampliar o compartilhamento de informações e os exercícios militares conjuntos. O pacto de resposta a possíveis ataques com armas de destruição em massa firmado pelas duas nações é uma “declaração explícita de confronto”, de acordo com Pyongyan.

Segundo o governo norte-coreano, o acordo pressupõe o uso de armas nucleares, biológicas e químicas contra a Coreia do Norte em uma eventual crise na Península Coreana. Para Pyongyang, a medida aumenta o risco de emprego de armas de destruição em massa na região.

Autoridades de defesa dos EUA e da Coreia do Sul se reuniram em Seul na semana passada para discutir formas de responder às ameaças representadas pelo programa nuclear norte-coreano.

A reunião foi conduzida por Woo Kyung-suk, diretor-geral do departamento de planejamento de políticas do Ministério da Defesa sul-coreano, e Jason Hamm, vice-secretário-assistente de Defesa dos EUA para políticas de dissuasão nuclear.

Segundo os governos, os programas bélicos da Coreia do Norte contribuem para a instabilidade na Península Coreana e em outras partes da região. EUA e Coreia do Sul concordaram ainda em manter a cooperação para responder a ameaças biológicas, incluindo doenças infecciosas como a Covid-19.

Pyongyang rejeita os apelos para abandonar seu arsenal nuclear.]

articles.title: IFMT abre 75 vagas para graduação a distância; veja como se inscrever | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições vão até 20 de setembro e podem ser feitas com notas do Enem ou histórico escolar; oportunidades estão distribuídas em sete polos.
articles.summary: Inscrições vão até 20 de setembro e podem ser feitas com notas do Enem ou histórico escolar; oportunidades estão distribuídas em sete polos.
articles.body:
As oportunidades estão distribuídas entre sete polos de apoio presencial em Mato Grosso e Goiás — Foto: Reprodução

O Instituto Federal de Mato Grosso (IFMT) está com 75 vagas abertas para o curso superior de Tecnologia em Sistemas para Internet, na modalidade de ensino a distância, para o segundo semestre de 2026. As oportunidades estão distribuídas entre sete polos de apoio presencial em Mato Grosso e Goiás, e as inscrições podem ser feitas até 20 de setembro .

Há duas formas de seleção. Em uma delas, o candidato pode usar a nota do Enem realizado entre 2010 e 2025. Na outra, a classificação será feita a partir do histórico escolar do ensino médio.

As oportunidades são distribuídas da seguinte forma:

O Edital nº 82/2026 prevê a seleção com base nas notas do Enem. Nesse caso, não é cobrada taxa de inscrição . O candidato precisa informar corretamente qual edição do exame, entre 2010 e 2025, será considerada na classificação.

Já o Edital nº 94/2026 utiliza as notas do histórico escolar do ensino médio, considerando disciplinas da Base Nacional Comum Curricular cursadas no 1º e no 2º ano. Para essa modalidade, a inscrição custa R$ 50 . Há possibilidade de isenção para candidatos que atendam aos critérios socioeconômicos previstos na legislação e para inscritos no CadÚnico. O histórico escolar deve ser anexado em formato PDF durante a inscrição.

Do total de vagas, 60% são destinadas a candidatos que fizeram todo o ensino médio em escolas públicas, conforme as regras de ações afirmativas.

As demais oportunidades são destinadas à ampla concorrência e a candidatos que estudaram em escolas particulares. Os editais também estabelecem reservas específicas considerando critérios como renda familiar, pertencimento a grupos PPI (pretos, pardos, indígenas e quilombolas) e pessoas com deficiência (PcD).

As inscrições para as duas modalidades terminam em 20 de setembro de 2026. Os candidatos devem consultar os editais completos no portal de seleções do IFMT antes de fazer a inscrição. Os documentos trazem informações sobre o cronograma, envio de documentos, procedimentos de heteroidentificação, matrícula e regras específicas de cada polo.

articles.title: Batida entre vans interdita rodovia em Pederneiras | G1
articles.standfirst: Uma das vans pegou fogo após a colisão traseira, mas ninguém ficou ferido. Trecho ficou totalmente interditado por cerca de uma hora e chegou a registrar 1 km de congestionamento.
articles.summary: Acidente na Rodovia Comandante João Ribeiro de Barros causou interdição total e congestionamento após colisão entre duas vans com incêndio em Pederneiras.
articles.body:
O km 222 da Rodovia Comandante João Ribeiro de Barros, em Pederneiras (SP), precisou ser totalmente interditado na noite desta terça-feira (15) após um acidente envolvendo duas vans.

Segundo a Agência Reguladora de Transporte de SP (Artesp), o motorista de uma das vans contou que se aproximou rapidamente do outro veículo e não conseguiu frear a tempo, provocando uma colisão traseira.

Van pegou fogo após a batida em Pederneiras — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Após a batida, a van atingida pegou fogo. O motorista conseguiu deixar o veículo sem ferimentos. No outro veículo, outras duas pessoas também não se machucaram.

A pista ficou totalmente interditada por cerca de uma hora para o atendimento da ocorrência. De acordo com a Artesp, o acidente provocou aproximadamente 1 km de congestionamento.

O trecho já foi liberado para o tráfego.

Van pega fogo após batida na Comandante João Ribeiro de Barros em Pederneiras — Foto: CCM Artesp/ Divulgação

Vans se envolveram uma colisão traseira na rodovia em Pederneiras — Foto: CCM Artesp / Divulgação

articles.title: Entenda relação do cantor inglês Seal com a Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo viralizou nas redes sociais. Na gravação, o jovem aparece com a camisa do Esporte Clube Bahia.
articles.summary: Filho do artista usava camisa de time de Salvador ao ganhar Ferrari. Vídeo viralizou nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
O filho do cantor inglês Seal, voz dos sucessos "Kiss From a Rose" e "Stand By Me", chamou a atenção nas redes sociais ao publicar um vídeo com a camisa do Esporte Clube Bahia, time de Salvador . A escolha da peça não foi aleatória: o britânico tem relações familiares com a capital baiana.

Na gravação, o garoto de 21 anos aparece ganhando uma Ferrari da mãe e do padrasto. A peça usada faz parte da coleção do time para a Copa do Mundo de 2022. (Veja o vídeo acima)

Seal durante show no Rock in Rio em 2015 — Foto: Fábio Tito/G1

Certo, mas onde entra a relação com a Bahia? O bisavô de Seal nasceu em Salvador. O artista falou sobre a relação com a Bahia em entrevista ao g1 em 2019, quando se preparava para se apresentar no Rock in Rio.

Na época, ele explicou que não teve relação direta com o bisavô, mas que sente uma forte relação com a música da Bahia.

"Sinto essa música em mim de alguma forma. No fim das contas, o tipo de músico que eu gosto e as qualidades dos artistas brasileiro que admiro, vêm muito da Bahia. Eu gosto muito do Dorival Caymmi", disse na ocasião.

Heidi Klum e o namorado, Tom Kaulitz, durante evento da amfAR, em maio de 2018 — Foto: REUTERS/Stephane Mahe

Henry Samuel, o jovem presenteado com uma Ferrari, é rodeado de celebridades. O garoto é filho de Seal com a modelo alemã Heidi Klum. Ela conhecida por ter trabalhado na Victoria's Secret e pelos realities show Project Runway e America's Got Talent.

Heidi e Seal foram casados por sete anos e tiveram quatro filhos. O casal anunciou a separação em 2012.

Em 2019, Heidi passou a se relacionar com o guitarrista alemão Tom Kaulitz, integrante da banda Tokio Hotel.

A Ferrari de Henry Samuel foi comprada por ele, após prometer o carro em uma aposta quando o enteado ainda era criança.

Veja mais notícias do estado no g1 Bahia .

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3058: 15 apostas de AL acertam quadra, veja resultado | G1
articles.body:
15 apostas de Alagoas acertaram a quadra no concurso 3058 da Mega-Sena, que teve o sorteio realizado na terça-feira (15), em São Paulo. Nenhuma aposta do Brasil acertou as seis dezenas e o prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 102 milhões.

Em Alagoas, as apostas ganhadoras são da capital, Agreste, Zona da Mata e Sertão do estado. Todos os vencedores levaram prêmios de R$1.185,36 O próximo sorteio será nesta quinta-feira (17).

Os números sorteados foram: 14- 23- 53- 56- 57- 60.

Confira apostas ganhadoras da Mega-Sena 3058

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo. A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

Bilhetes da Mega-Sena, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada.

Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Pak Navy vessel collides with Indian Navy ship, MEA summons Islamabad’s diplomat
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: A Pakistan navy ship has collided with an Indian warship in the Arabian Sea.“On the evening of Sept 15, a Pakistan Naval Ship closed a fron.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Pakistan navy ship has collided with an Indian warship in the Arabian Sea.“On the evening of Sept 15, a Pakistan Naval Ship closed a frontline Indian Naval warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea at high speed, manoeuvring in an unprofessional and unsafe manner. This led to a collision,” a source told TOI. However, the source said, “No damage has been reported.”New Delhi has summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires (CDA) after the incident. “The CDA was summoned to the Ministry of External Affairs today and a strong protest was lodged with him over the unacceptable and unprofessional conduct of Pakistani naval units at sea that led to a collision with a unit of the Indian Navy," the MEA said.The MEA said the diplomat was advised to convey to the Pakistani authorities concerned the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents.“While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” it said.

articles.title: In 1944, SS John Barry sank carrying 3 million Saudi silver riyals; salvors recovered more than 1 million, a 16-ton haul expected to fetch at least $20 million
articles.summary: US News: The SS John Barry sank in 1944 carrying 3 million Saudi silver riyals, and a salvage operation recovered over 1 million coins now valued at $20 million. Discover the captivating history behind the sinking and the ongoing search for the remaining treasure.
articles.body: More than 1 million Saudi silver riyals were brought up from the wreck of the SS John Barry in 1994, roughly five decades after the American Liberty ship sank off Oman with 3 million of the coins in its holds. Nearly 16 tons of the recovered silver were headed for a Sotheby’s auction by the following year,, where the lot was expected to fetch at least $20 million.The ship had been carrying the coins to Saudi Arabia during the final years of World War II, and the riyals had been minted in Philadelphia at the request of Saudi Arabia and were intended to help pay workers who were involved in the rapidly developing oil industry. The cargo was kept secret enough that the crew was not aware of the coins, according to the 1995 Associated Press report published by The Christian Science Monitor. The John Barry was torpedoed by a German submarine in November 1944 and sank in the Arabian Sea. Most of its roughly 70 crew members were rescued, while two died. The ship eventually became the target of a specialized recovery operation that involved a modified drilling vessel and equipment that was capable of reaching the wreck on the seabed. The operation reached the cargo hold in late 1994, and the salvors began bringing silver coins to the surface.The coins stayed underwater for half a centuryA detailed account was published by AramcoWorld and records that the salvage operation began in October 1994 by making use of the modified drilling ship Flex LD and a 50-ton video-equipped grab designed by the French research organization IFREMER. The equipment was lowered through more than a mile of water to reach the wreck. In early November, the first silver was identified on the video feed, and over the next five days, about 1.3 million Saudi riyals were recovered, weighing approximately 17 tons.The operation reached only some parts of the wreck and cargo spaces, which left a large quantity of the original shipment underwater. The origin of the recovered coins gave them a historical value beyond the metal itself, and Sotheby’s planned to sell the recovered group as a single lot.The Christian Science Monitor reported in November 1995 that more than 1 million of the recovered coins, which weighed almost 16 tons, were expected to bring at least $20 million. Sotheby’s said the coins were being sold together because of their historical association with the wreck.The coins had been ordered for Saudi Arabia at a time when the kingdom needed currency to pay workers, including those involved in the construction of oil facilities. The shipment was therefore part of the financial infrastructure supporting Saudi Arabia’s emerging oil economy.The wreck remains tied to a second silver mysteryAnother claim that was linked to the wreck concerned a much larger quantity of silver bullion that was allegedly aboard the ship, and the existence and ownership of that bullion became the subject of later salvage disputes. A 2026 federal court opinion that reviewed litigation over the wreck records that the ship sank on August 28, 1944, carrying 3 million U.S.-minted Saudi one-riyal coins. The court record states that the first major salvage expedition in 1994 recovered about 1.4 million of the coins but found no evidence of the separate silver bullion that had been the subject of later claims. The recovered riyals are documented cargo, while the alleged bullion has remained disputed. The court record also shows that salvage rights to the vessel had been awarded in 1989, before the 1994 recovery effort.Heritage Auctions has sold salvaged examples described as Philadelphia-minted Saudi riyals from the wreck. The coins recovered in the 1990s therefore did not disappear into a single historical collection, since some have continued circulating among collectors decades after they were lifted from the seabed.The original cargo, however, remains only partly recovered. The 3 million coins that went down with the John Barry were divided between what was brought to the surface in the 1990s and what remains associated with the wreck. The ship that disappeared beneath the Arabian Sea in 1944 still has a portion of its wartime cargo on the seabed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: An ancient British farming craft faded after World War II; now 2,500 farmers want to revive 1,300km of mature hedgerows to help wildlife and reduce flooding
articles.summary: UK News: It's seeing a revival and how. The ancient craft of hedge laying is back in trend among farmers as they are using the technique dating back to 18th an.
articles.body: It's seeing a revival and how. The ancient craft of hedge laying is back in trend among farmers as they are using the technique dating back to 18th and 19th centuries in order to boost wildlife, capture carbon and help tackle flooding. Hedge laying which restores and revives mature hedges to keep them fresh was among the four most popular categories of capital grants selected by farmers out of a total pot of £225m provided by the government this year to support practical environmental improvements on farms and across the countryside.The 2,500 farmers across England who applied for grants to restore and maintain their mature hedgerows using the craft that dates back to thousands of year will lay 1,300 km of mature hedgerows, if the grants are approved. According to Megan Gimber, the key habitats officer for the People's Trust for Endangered Species said that hedge laying was one of the most effective tools farmers had to respond to the climate crisis. “Hedge laying really stopped after the war, so it has been over a generation since it was a normal part of farm management and we have seen a huge decline in hedgerows as a result,” she said.“These grants will give 1,300km of potentially ancient hedges a new lease of life, to help plug the gap, and it is fantastic that it is such a popular grant application.”Mature, maintained hedgerows are a carbon sink that capture more carbon in every hectare than forests. They support thousands of species, provide shade for livestock, reduce soil erosion and slow down, absorb and store vast amounts of rainwater to help reduce flooding. “They are massively important,” said Stephen Budding, the chair of the National Hedgelaying Society. “The greatest biodiversity gain is from hedge laying older hedges. “Our members are seeing quite a surge in work, but I don’t think this would be happening without the government grants available.”The art of hedge layingHedge laying involves cutting through the hedge stems almost completely, then laying them at an angle to the ground. Laying the branches down invigorates growth at the point where they have been cut, filling gaps in the hedges and restoring youth and freshness.The craft is done by hand by skilled layers, many of whom will also be competing next month at the National Hedgelaying Championships in Chipping Norton. It was extremely common until World War II, post which there was a massive shift toward industrialised farming, cheap manufactured fencing and also severe shortage of labour.Robert Rose, who farms 220 acres of grassland for beef cattle and arable fields at Rosewood Farm in Ellerton in Yorkshire’s Lower Derwent valley, is waiting for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) to approve his application for a grant to lay old blackthorn, newer hawthorn and ash and willow hedges across his farm. “We lay the hedges in a modern conservation style that retains more of the bushy growth for the benefit of nesting birds as well as stock proofing,” said Rose, who farms with his brother and wife.The trio planted new hedges about 20 years ago, but maintaining them is vital to keep them working to store carbon, support wildlife and retain water. “We taught ourselves how to do the laying, which was a bit of trial and error,” he said. “It is only recently that we have noticed how much other farmers are talking about hedge laying online, in community groups, it really seems to be taking off.” The grant Rose has applied for will aid him in laying about 50 metres of hedges along with planting new hedgerows and coppicing others. Peak hedge laying season starts in October and ends in February, so farmers like Rose are hoping for quick decisions from Defra. “There are so many benefits with hedge laying for wildlife, for livestock, for conservation. We see a lot more birds using the hedges and a lot more small mammals around the bottom of mature managed hedges,” said Rose.Along with grant requests for hedge laying, about 5,000 applications are for planting new hedges, representing approximately 2,500 km of new hedgerows. But these will not survive without management. The centre also discovered that 61% of the newly planted hedges surveyed existed as hedges in their 2007 survey, but had since been lost and required replanting.“Hedgerows are succession habitats, made up of trees and shrubby woody species, that naturally change over time,” said Gimber. “They require management to maintain the valuable mid-succession stage of bushy, low growth and prevent them developing into lines of trees.”“This government is putting its full weight behind farmers – giving them the funding, tools and opportunities they need to succeed. In July, we opened a new round of environmental land management capital grants with increased funding of up to £225m available to support investment in infrastructure that boosts productivity, strengthens resilience and supports environmental outcomes, which has now closed following strong uptake,” said a Defra spokesperson.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 20 dead, dozens missing after war-damaged apartment block collapses in Gaza
articles.summary: Middle East News: Gaza rescuers on Wednesday searched through the wreckage of a bomb-damaged apartment building that collapsed overnight in Gaza City. The incident kill.
articles.body: Gaza rescuers on Wednesday searched through the wreckage of a bomb-damaged apartment building that collapsed overnight in Gaza City. The incident killed at least 20 Palestinians, including five children, and left nearly 100 people feared trapped under the rubble.The seven-storey building collapsed in the Tal al-Hawa area, where at least 10 families were living. Fourteen people were injured in the collapse, while rescue workers continued searching for survivors.Raed Al-Dahshan, director of Gaza City's civil defence service, said rescuers could still hear people beneath the debris."We are still hearing voices from under the rubble, so there is still hope to find people," said Dahshan.Video obtained by Reuters showed rescue workers trying to pull two people from beneath a collapsed wall. Another video circulating on social media showed Gaza civil defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal carrying a young girl wrapped in a blood-stained scarf.Rescue efforts have been slowed by a lack of heavy machinery and other equipment needed to clear the rubble safely. Residents have also joined civil defence teams in digging through the debris by hand.Alessandro Mrakic, head of the UN Development Programme's Gaza office, said rescuers from some UN agencies were involved in the operation, along with Egypt's relief agency."The situation, as you see, is tragic because we don't have the equipment and machinery that is needed. So there are actually people that are digging with their bare hands. We need to prepare (for more deaths)," said Mrakic.Mrakic said hundreds of other buildings were also at risk."There are approximately 400 buildings at risk of collapse. And we know that these buildings will collapse, especially now with the upcoming winter," he added.The collapse has highlighted the dangers facing thousands of Palestinians who have moved into damaged buildings because of a severe shortage of shelters and tents. Gaza's local rescue service estimates that about 2,000 damaged buildings are still inhabited by families.Dahshan said at least 10 families had been living in the collapsed building and warned residents against entering damaged structures."The limited availability of shelter options forced residents to move into this building, believing it was safe. However, at one point it collapsed entirely, tragically crashing down on people as they slept," said Dahshan.Many families have told Reuters in recent months that they were living in partially damaged buildings to protect themselves from wind and rain. The shortage of new tents has also left many people with few alternatives.Palestinian and UN officials have blamed Israeli restrictions on the entry of heavy machinery for the difficulties faced by rescue teams. Israel says the restrictions are intended to prevent such equipment from reaching militant groups.The building collapse is also part of a wider problem across Gaza, where thousands of structures have been damaged or partially destroyed during the war. The UN estimates that Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas' deadly attack on Israel in October 2023, has generated around 61 million tonnes of rubble and debris. It could take seven years to clear it.An October 2025 US-backed ceasefire halted large-scale fighting in Gaza, but Israeli strikes have continued and negotiations over a lasting peace have made little progress.Hamas has accused Israel of violating the ceasefire and obstructing US President Donald Trump's broader plan to end the conflict. The plan includes an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and the disarmament of Hamas. Israel, meanwhile, has accused Hamas of violating the agreement.More than 1,300 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to health officials in the territory. The Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed during the same period.Hamas does not usually disclose information on fatalities among its fighters.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1993, Virginia buried 1.7 million discarded tyres beneath a highway near Williamsburg; a decade later, engineers found the road was still performing well
articles.summary: US News: Discover how Virginia ingeniously transformed 1.7 million discarded tyres into a durable highway embankment near Williamsburg. This groundbreaking project not only resolved a serious waste issue but also proved effective over a decade of monitoring, showcasing a sustainable path for waste tyre disposal.
articles.body: Getting rid of one old tyre is relatively easy, but eliminating millions of them is a different problem altogether. Tyres in stockpiles do not break down; they collect rainwater that becomes a breeding ground for mosquitoes, and large stockpiles of them have a history of catching fire and burning for weeks at a time, producing thick, oily smoke that is hard to put out and worse to breathe. Virginia had exactly that kind of waste-tire backlog when engineers decided to turn part of the problem into a potential construction material.The Virginia Department of Environmental Quality conducted a comprehensive statewide survey that found 1,331 tire piles containing more than 25 million waste tires. Rather than send all that rubber to the landfill, the Virginia Department of Transportation partnered with the state’s environmental regulators and the Virginia Transportation Research Council on an experimental project to determine whether shredded tyres could be used as a construction material for new roads.Turning scrap rubber into road fillAlthough Virginia's attempt was on a far greater scale, the concept itself was not wholly novel. In the summer of 1993, construction workers used shredded tyre material, referred to as "tyre derived aggregate" in engineering circles, to build an embankment for a bridge approach near Williamsburg in York County. In place of the sand, gravel, or crushed stone that typically make up the majority of a highway embankment, workers put in about 1.7 million discarded tyres, chopped into pieces and occasionally combined with dirt to aid drainage and compaction.Aggregate made from tyres has several truly practical engineering qualities. It drains water more easily, which can help minimise damage from frost, and it is significantly lighter than soil, which lessens the strain an embankment places on the land beneath it.Watching, testing and waiting for 10 yearsResearchers monitored the site for the next ten years, measuring how the embankment settled and whether it continued to perform structurally. They also sampled groundwater from wells around the embankment to check whether metals or other substances from the shredded rubber were entering the water.But maybe more importantly, scientists watched the environment around them intently. At various times the groundwater was sampled from wells located above and below the embankment. Special attention was paid to the possible seepage of metals or other substances that might leach from the rubber to the water table. This was the most important feature to the sceptics of the idea.The verdict after ten yearsBy 2004, the Virginia Transportation Research Council had a full decade of data, and the conclusions were more encouraging than worrisome. The final report, Field Study of a Shredded-tire Embankment in Virginia, was published in 2004 after a 10-year monitoring period and found that the shredded-tire embankment performed satisfactorily based on environmental and engineering assessments.Based on those results, the researchers proposed that shredded tyre embankments be investigated as a viable, environmentally friendly method of disposing of waste tyres elsewhere in the state. The Williamsburg project was a huge success, leading to a much larger cleanup effort. According to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, the state has now assisted in the removal or beneficial reuse of around 22.9 million discarded tyres from the heaps identified in that first 1993 assessment, with just a small percentage of the original stockpiles remaining today.What began as a very desperate approach to an increasing waste problem turned out to show something more beneficial than a one-off remedy. Over a decade, data collection tested and monitored the idea: a material many people would associate with scrapyard fires proved capable of supporting a highway embankment for years.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 and Optimus GX 7100 SSDs now available in India: Check price, specs and more
articles.summary: Tech News News: SanDisk has expanded its internal SSD portfolio in India with the launch of the Optimus GX Pro 8100 NVMe SSD and Optimus GX 7100 NVMe SSD. The new sto.
articles.body: SanDisk has expanded its internal SSD portfolio in India with the launch of the Optimus GX Pro 8100 NVMe SSD and Optimus GX 7100 NVMe SSD. The new storage drives target gamers, creators, developers, and professionals with demanding workloads, including gaming, content creation, and AI apps.The Optimus GX Pro 8100 is positioned as the higher-performance option, using a PCIe 5.0 interface and offering capacities of up to 8TB. Meanwhile, the Optimus GX 7100 targets laptops and handhelds with PCIe 4.0 performance and capacities of up to 4TB. Here are the prices, availability and specifications of the drives.SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100, GX 7100: Price and availability in IndiaThe SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 NVMe SSD is now available in India through Amazon. The 1TB variant without a heatsink is priced at Rs 34,999. The company has not specified pricing for the higher-capacity variants in the announcement.The SanDisk Optimus GX 7100 NVMe SSD is also available on Amazon in India. Its 1TB variant is priced at Rs 26,799. The drive is available in capacities ranging from 500GB to 4TB.SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100, GX 7100: Key specs and featuresSanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100The Optimus GX Pro 8100 is the more performance-focused model in the new lineup. It uses a PCIe 5.0 interface and offers sequential read speeds of up to 14,900MB/s, while sequential write speeds can reach 14,000MB/s. This is aimed at demanding workloads where faster data access and transfers are important.The SSD is available in capacities of up to 8TB, with the 8TB model offering up to 4,800 TBW (terabytes written). This makes it suited to workloads involving frequent data writes, including professional apps and content creation.SanDisk is also offering the drive with an anodised aluminium heatsink, designed to help manage heat during sustained workloads.SanDisk Optimus GX 7100The Optimus GX 7100 uses a PCIe 4.0 x4 interface and is designed for gaming and creative apps, particularly on laptops and handheld devices. It supports sequential read speeds of up to 7,250MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 6,900MB/s on the 1TB and 2TB models.The SSD comes in capacities ranging from 500GB to 4TB, giving users multiple options for storing games, apps and creative files. It also features nCache 4.0 technology, which SanDisk says supports responsive gameplay and demanding everyday apps.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: In 2008, scientists removed invasive rats from Alaska's Hawadax Island; 11 years later, seabirds returned and the kelp ecosystem recovered
articles.summary: US News: Alaska's Hawadax Island, once known as Rat Island, offers one of conservation's clearest success stories. Invasive Norway rats, accidentally introduce.
articles.body: Alaska's Hawadax Island, once known as Rat Island, offers one of conservation's clearest success stories. Invasive Norway rats, accidentally introduced by 18th-century shipwrecks and wartime shipping traffic, wiped out nesting seabirds and unravelled the island's rocky intertidal food web for two centuries. In 2008, scientists carried out a full eradication, removing every rat from the island. Eleven years later, a 2021 study titled ‘Indirect effects of invasive rat removal result in recovery of island rocky intertidal community structure’ in Scientific Reports confirmed seabirds had returned, and with them, a kelp-rich intertidal ecosystem resembling untouched islands nearby.Invasive rats devastated Hawadax Island's seabird populationNorway rats reached the Aleutian Islands through 18th-century shipwrecks and World War II military activity, eventually overrunning dozens of islands in what became known as the "Rat Islands." On Hawadax, the rats became a new apex predator, preying heavily on shorebird eggs and chicks. Breeding seabird populations collapsed, removing the island's main check on herbivorous intertidal invertebrates like snails and limpets. Freed from predation, these grazers multiplied and stripped away fleshy algae and kelp. Researcher Carolyn Kurle and colleagues documented this rat-dominated baseline during 2008 surveys, capturing a shoreline ecosystem badly out of balance before any restoration work began on the island.How the 2008 rat eradication on Hawadax Island startedAccording to Island Conservation, in 2008, a coordinated eradication effort led by Island Conservation, the US Fish and Wildlife Service, and The Nature Conservancy removed invasive rats from the island entirely, and it was renamed Hawadax, reviving its original Aleut name meaning "the island over there with two knolls." The project gave researchers an unusual opportunity; they had pre-eradication data from 2008, allowing direct comparison against later surveys. Follow-up visits in 2013 showed early signs of recovery, while a comprehensive 2019 survey, five and eleven years after removal respectively, let scientists track the island's ecological trajectory against neighbouring islands that had never hosted rats at all.The seabirds return and rebuild the food webWith rats gone, native shorebirds such as black oystercatchers and rock sandpipers began nesting successfully again, rebuilding populations that had nearly vanished under rat predation. As seabird numbers climbed, they resumed their historic role as apex predators of the rocky intertidal zone, once again consuming snails, limpets, and other herbivorous invertebrates in large numbers. This reestablished a three-level trophic cascade birds, invertebrates, algae, that had been disrupted for over two centuries by the rats acting as an unnatural fourth predatory tier. Lead author Carolyn Kurle noted the team expected recovery to take longer, calling the pace of the seabird rebound genuinely surprising. “We were surprised that the level of recovery unfolded so quickly, we thought it could be longer,” she said.Kelp ecosystem recovery confirms the chain reaction on trophic levelsAs invertebrate grazing pressure fell, fleshy algae and kelp cover expanded significantly across Hawadax's shoreline, and by 2019 the intertidal community closely resembled that of islands that had never been invaded by rats. The Scientific Reports study, led by UC San Diego's Carolyn Kurle with researchers from UC Santa Cruz, Island Conservation, and federal agencies, called it a rare, measurable example of conservation success. Co-author Donald Croll noted the work confirms how deeply introduced predators can reshape entire island ecosystems, while also showing the scale of benefits removal can deliver. The findings offer strong evidence for continued rat-eradication efforts on invaded islands worldwide, from remote Alaska to the tropics.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pak vessel PNS Hunain involved in collision with Indian Navy ship - all about Yarmook-class corvette
articles.summary: International News: The Pakistani naval vessel involved in a collision with an Indian Navy ship in the North Arabian Sea on Tuesday evening was PNS Hunain, a Yarmook-clas.
articles.body: The Pakistani naval vessel involved in a collision with an Indian Navy ship in the North Arabian Sea on Tuesday evening was PNS Hunain, a Yarmook-class corvette of the Pakistan Navy, sources were quoted as saying by news agency ANI.According to sources, the incident took place on September 15 when the Pakistani vessel approached a frontline Indian Navy warship that was carrying out a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea.What is the Yarmook-class corvette?PNS Hunain (F-273) is a Yarmook-class corvette operated by the Pakistan Navy and was built by Damen Shipyards in Galati, Romania.The class comprises multi-role vessels designed for coastal defence, patrol and maritime security operations, with surveillance and firepower capabilities for missions in the Arabian Sea and along coastal areas.The Yarmook-class corvettes have a displacement of about 2,300 tonnes, a length of 91.3 metres and a crew of around 60 personnel.They are powered by four Caterpillar 3516 diesel engines in a combined diesel and diesel (CODAD) configuration and can reach a maximum speed of 22 knots. The vessels have a range of about 6,000 nautical miles at 12 knots and an endurance of up to 40 days.Armament and aviation capabilitiesThe Yarmook-class corvettes are equipped with a mix of guns, missile systems and close-in defence weapons. Their armament includes one 30 mm Aselsan SMASH remote weapon station and two 12.7 mm Aselsan STAMP remote weapon stations.The vessels are also fitted with two four-cell launchers for Harbah surface-to-surface missiles, which are part of the Babur missile family. For close-range defence against aerial and other threats, they carry one 20 mm Phalanx Block 1B close-in weapon system (CIWS).The ships can also operate one helicopter and one unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), extending their surveillance and maritime reconnaissance capabilities.What happened in Arabian Sea?The Pakistani naval ship closed in at high speed and manoeuvred in an "unprofessional and unsafe manner", resulting in a collision, sources said. No major damage was reported in the incident.Following the incident, India on Wednesday summoned the Charge d'Affaires of the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over what it termed the "unacceptable and unprofessional conduct" of Pakistani naval units."The Charge d'Affaires of the High Commission for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan in New Delhi was summoned to the Ministry of External Affairs today and a strong protest was lodged with him over the unacceptable and unprofessional conduct of Pakistani naval units at sea that led to a collision with a unit of the Indian Navy," the ministry of external affairs said in a statement.

articles.title: Indian warship rammed by Pakistani naval vessel: How grey-zone tactics are entering the Arabian Sea
articles.summary: News News: A Pakistani Navy ship collided with an Indian Navy vessel in the Northern Arabian Sea on Tuesday evening. The Indian ship was on a routine mission whe.
articles.body: A Pakistani Navy ship collided with an Indian Navy vessel in the Northern Arabian Sea on Tuesday evening. The Indian ship was on a routine mission when it was approached by a Pakistani naval ship at high speeds. A source in the Indian Navy has stated that the Pakistani ship maneuvered in an unprofessional and unsafe manner, leading to a collision and that no damage has been reported. Another source in the navy has stated that the incident has been against the mutually decided confidence building measures and hence the issue has been raised diplomatically.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has summoned the Pakistani Charge d'Affairs over the incident and has also instructed the Indian Charge d'Affairs in Islamabad to raise thew issue with the government there. This is the second such incident to have come to light since 2011, when Pakistani warship PNS Babur rammed in to an Indian navy vessel in the northern part of the Arabian Sea, that time too the incident was raised with Pakistan on a diplomatic level.Ramming at seaRamming as a tactic of war at sea, is almost as old as naval warfare itself. Naval ramming has ancient roots, with the Romans and Greeks both relying on it as a core weapon, the Roman rostrum fitted onto galleys, and Greek triremes built specifically for the tactic. Interestingly, ancient China never developed similar ramming ships, since the flat-bottomed junk's design, lacking a proper keel, simply wasn't suited to an elongated underwater spur.The first modern instance of ramming between major warships came during the American Civil War, at the 1862 Battle of Hampton Roads, when the armoured Confederate vessel CSS Virginia rammed and swiftly sank the Union frigate Cumberland.The tactic resurfaced through both World Wars, claiming numerous ships and submarines. Perhaps its most famous instance involves PT-109, sunk during the Solomon Islands campaign, commanded at the time by a young John F Kennedy, who later became US President.Ramming even found its way into a far less lethal but oddly memorable chapter of naval history, the so-called Cod Wars between Iceland and the UK, fought over fishing rights in the North Atlantic, where ramming became something of a recurring, almost theatrical tactic between rival patrol vessels.Also read: Pak vessel PNS Hunain involved in collision with Indian Navy ship - all about Yarmook-class corvettePak employs China's grey war tacticChina's use of ramming and water cannons in the South China Sea sits at the heart of a growing debate around grey zone warfare, tactics that stay deliberately below the threshold of open conflict while still advancing strategic goals. Beijing has leaned on its Coast Guard and maritime militia to ram vessels and blast rivals with high-pressure water cannons, exploiting legal ambiguity to solidify illegal territorial claims without triggering a formal military response, similar to the salami slicing tactic used in Eastern Ladakh and elsewhere.A report from the US based think-tank RAND corporation argues that this calculated ambiguity needs to end. When ramming with reinforced hulls or close-range water cannon use causes damage comparable to conventional kinetic force, a missile strike or torpedo attack, it should be treated as a grave use of force, justifying a proportionate kinetic response in self-defence.What the law saysThe collision between an Indian Navy ship and a Pakistani naval vessel in international waters has raised questions over Pakistan’s conduct at sea and the broader India-Pakistan confidence-building framework. New Delhi has also said the conduct was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the 1991 agreement governing advance notice of military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements.The incident also brings back into focus an important but unfinished commitment made in the 1999 Lahore Declaration. The declaration called for discussions on an agreement to prevent incidents involving the naval and air forces of the two countries. Such an agreement was intended to reduce the possibility of accidents, miscalculations and dangerous encounters between their military forces.The wider purpose of the Lahore process was to establish practical mechanisms for reducing military risks between two nuclear-armed neighbours. Several confidence-building measures followed, but the proposed maritime incidents agreement was never concluded, but India and Pakistan ended up fighting for the Kargil heights a few months later.
